item.title: security: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence observed threat actors using the agentic offensive security framework ARTEX to search GitHub for exposed OAuth application secrets. Compromised OAuth applications were then used to carry out authenticated actions inside affected organizations’ tenants.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed a compromise affecting LiteLLM 1.107.0 that used Python startup hooks to steal credentials and load remote code. The post also covers detections and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: NeedyMantis: Unpacking a post-compromise malware family used in targeted operations
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified NeedyMantis, a modular post-compromise malware framework used in targeted intrusions. It uses custom loaders, encrypted archives, and extensible components to keep access and support follow-on activity.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: TerminalFix campaign deploys a reverse tunnel through multistage intrusion
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed the TerminalFix ClickFix campaign, which uses fake CAPTCHA prompts, DLL sideloading, and a reverse tunnel in a multistage intrusion. The post includes detections and hunting guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
